scientific_question: Can the official Hindsight uv.lock be exported with a frozen, project-owned uv binary without mutating a shared Python environment or re-resolving package versions?
decision_informed: Whether an exact third-party dependency artifact plan can be produced before Hindsight environment installation.
scientific_evidence_role: dependency-tool acquisition evidence only; no package resolution change, dependency installation, import, model, service, lifecycle, numerical, superiority, or SOTA claim is permitted

official_release.source: Astral official GitHub releases API and release checksum sidecar

execution_contract.wave1_non_interference: This bounded tool-only acquisition may run during Wave-1 because it cannot access models, datasets, dependency environments, APIs, pg0, or GPUs and its network rate is capped.

acceptance: The checksum sidecar matches its frozen byte count and SHA-256 and names the frozen archive hash.
The archive matches its frozen byte count and SHA-256.
The archive contains exactly one directory plus regular uv and uvx files with no links or path traversal.
The extracted uv binary reports exactly uv 0.12.9.
Both binary sizes and SHA-256 values are retained.
The evidence root has TERMINAL_ACCEPTED, no TERMINAL_REJECTED, and a verified evidence inventory.
failure: Any collision, download failure, byte or hash mismatch, unsafe archive member, extraction error, or version mismatch seals a fresh TERMINAL_REJECTED evidence root and retains all partial artifacts.
next_gate_after_acceptance: Independently audit the tool, then export the accepted source uv.lock with --frozen, --no-dev, --package hindsight-all, and --no-emit-workspace. Export only; do not install packages until Wave-1 releases the resource gate.
prohibited_actions: using an installer script or moving latest-version URL
executing downloaded content before archive hash and member validation
using uv to update uv.lock or resolve new versions
installing Python packages, downloading models, or changing shared environments
starting pg0, a service, lifecycle, or numerical evaluation
deleting or repairing a rejected root in place
populating any comparison-table numeric cell from this stage
